answer: Temporal work credit: each identity must complete a slow, verifiable task chain (e.g., a multi-day shale-logging series) before gaining transaction rights. Honest agents spend idle compute, costing little; attackers must duplicate that work per clone, paying full time and energy each time. A dune of accumulated delay throttles mass cloning, and every false identity burns a quill's worth of signed task history that cannot be transferred, making fakery costlier than acting honestly.
